answer_1.quote: we have selected two well-studied tasks from the literature: knowledge-grounded dialogue and abstractive summarization.

answer_2.quote: We use various evaluation metrics applied for knowledge grounding and natural language generation. We categorize the metrics into 3 categories: token-based, knowledge-based, and multifaceted. For token-based automatic metrics, we used BLEU-4, Rouge-L, ChrF, and METEOR... For knowledge-based metrics, we first used Knowledge-F1 (KF1)... and K-Copy... Finally, we also utilize UniEval... and for summarization, we take Coherence, Consistency, Fluency, Relevance... We also employ MFMA...

answer_4.quote: We randomly sampled 100 examples and asked 3 different evaluators to measure their fluency, relevance to the dialogue context, groundedness to reference knowledge, and if the response is an unnatural copy of the knowledge... The evaluators were asked to evaluate the summaries in 3 dimensions: fluency, groundedness, and completeness.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators measured fluency, relevance (for dialogue), groundedness, unnatural copy (for dialogue), and completeness (for summarization).
